item.title: UWF President Diaz Among DeSantis Associates Now Leading Florida Universities
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: University of West Florida President Manny Diaz Jr. is among a growing roster of DeSantis political allies and former staffers who have taken the helm of Florida's public universities and colleges, according to a social media post tracking the appointments. Diaz joins six other DeSantis-connected figures now serving as university presidents across…
item.content:encoded:
University of West Florida President Manny Diaz Jr. is among a growing roster of DeSantis political allies and former staffers who have taken the helm of Florida's public universities and colleges, according to a social media post tracking the appointments.

Diaz joins six other DeSantis-connected figures now serving as university presidents across the state, including Jeanette Nuñez at Florida International University, Richard Corcoran at New College of Florida, Marva Johnson at Florida A&M University, Adam Hasner at Florida Atlantic University, Alex Kelly at Pensacola State College, and Anastasios "Stasi" Kamoutsas at Polk State College.

The pattern reflects the governor's influence over higher education leadership in Florida. UWF appointed Diaz to its presidency in 2023, positioning him to oversee the Pensacola-area university as it navigates state education policy under the DeSantis administration. His tenure comes as Florida's higher education system faces significant policy shifts, including controversial curriculum and governance changes at state universities.

item.content:encoded:
Three new saltwater finfish records have been set in Mississippi during September, according to the state Department of Marine Resources. All three records were established using conventional tackle, the agency announced.

While the specific species and weights weren't detailed in the initial release, the accomplishments highlight the rich fishing opportunities available along the Mississippi Gulf Coast. The records come as fall fishing season brings optimal conditions for saltwater anglers throughout the region.

Fishermen in the broader Gulf area, including those based in Northwest Florida, often compete for similar records and frequently travel between Mississippi and Florida waters for prime fishing seasons. For anyone interested in pursuing their own records, both Mississippi and Florida maintain official record-keeping systems for saltwater catches.

item.title: Sen. Scott Introduces Bill to Block Foreign Child Predators from US Visas
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senator Rick Scott unveiled legislation Thursday aimed at strengthening vetting procedures for foreign visa applicants by giving federal agencies access to child exploitation databases. The SCREEN Act — Strengthened Checks for Reliable Evaluation of Entrants Nationwide — would allow the Department of Homeland Security and State Department to…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott unveiled legislation Thursday aimed at strengthening vetting procedures for foreign visa applicants by giving federal agencies access to child exploitation databases.

The SCREEN Act — Strengthened Checks for Reliable Evaluation of Entrants Nationwide — would allow the Department of Homeland Security and State Department to access records from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children during visa processing. Currently, that data is shared only with certain law enforcement agencies, a gap Scott says has allowed foreign workers with child sexual abuse material to slip through.

The bill was prompted by recent reports that cruise lines and other employers hired foreign workers on temporary C-1/D visas who were later found with child sexual abuse material. Scott called the current system a bureaucratic failure. "The greatest country in the history of the world should have 100% certainty that we aren't letting child predators come here on work visas," Scott said in a statement.

Representative Carlos Giménez introduced companion legislation in the House, with Senator Ted Budd as an original cosponsor. The lawmakers say interagency coordination is essential to both national security and protecting American children from exploitation.

item.title: HUD announces 9 fair housing discrimination charges
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development announced nine new charges of discrimination under the Fair Housing Act on Thursday, according to a press release from HUD's Office of Public Affairs. The charges involve violations across multiple protected categories. Four cases allege discrimination based on familial status, including…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development announced nine new charges of discrimination under the Fair Housing Act on Thursday, according to a press release from HUD's Office of Public Affairs.

The charges involve violations across multiple protected categories. Four cases allege discrimination based on familial status, including discriminatory rental practices affecting families with children. Three charges involve alleged disability discrimination, including failures to provide reasonable accommodations. One additional charge involves allegations of sexual harassment in housing.

The announcement reflects HUD's enforcement efforts under its Office of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity, which investigates and prosecutes housing discrimination cases. According to the release, the office has reduced its backlog of pending fair housing complaints by 46 percent since September 2025.

Fair Housing Act protections make it illegal for housing providers to discriminate based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, and disability. Anyone who believes they've experienced housing discrimination can file a complaint through HUD's website at hud.gov/reporthousingdiscrimination.

item.title: USPS Unveils New Kwanzaa Stamp Featuring Father, Daughter
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Postal Service is adding to its collection of Kwanzaa stamps with a new design unveiled today at the 111th annual conference of the Association for the Study of African American Life and History. The stamp features a digital illustration of a father and young daughter smiling at each other, both dressed in traditional African attire — he…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Postal Service is adding to its collection of Kwanzaa stamps with a new design unveiled today at the 111th annual conference of the Association for the Study of African American Life and History. The stamp features a digital illustration of a father and young daughter smiling at each other, both dressed in traditional African attire — he in a green, yellow and white dashiki with a matching kufi hat, she in a coordinating pink print dress with a flower in her hair and holding a wrapped gift.

The Kwanzaa stamp continues a tradition that began in 1997, with new designs released every two years since 2016. Previous stamps have depicted parents and children with Kwanzaa candles, harvests, and cultural celebrations. Matthew Toman, postmaster in Norfolk, Virginia, served as the dedicating official and praised the artistic vision behind the stamp. "With every new design, I continue to be amazed by the creativity of our artists and designers and their ability to capture the essence of Kwanzaa," Toman said.

Kwanzaa, observed annually from December 26 through January 1, was founded in the United States in 1966 to celebrate African American culture and unity. The week-long holiday centers on seven principles — unity, self-determination, collective work, cooperative economics, purpose, creativity and faith — each represented by one of seven candles in the traditional kinara, or candleholder. The holiday incorporates pan-African traditions of first-harvest celebrations and draws its name from the Swahili phrase "matunda ya kwanza," meaning "first fruits."

Kids can trick-or-treat among more than 200 local vendors, ride a Haunted Trolley between the two market locations and meet some creepy creatures during a live animal presentation.


Costumes are encouraged, and Winterfest’s Pumpkinhead will also make appearances. The market runs from nine a.m. until two, with admission and most activities free.

item.content:encoded: Pensacola is waking up to typical late September coastal weather Thursday morning, according to Florida Gulf Signal. At 8 a.m., conditions include easterly winds at 13.6 knots and an air temperature of 83.3 degrees. Visibility is limited due to low-contrast, dark skies over the water. A rising tide is expected to peak at 1.4 feet around 10:20 a.m., followed by a low tide of 0.8 feet at 7:22 p.m. Beach-goers and boaters should monitor local marine forecasts for any updates as the day progresses.
